written.myAnswer: Chemistry has a vast and varied subject matter; its division allows specialisation and makes the subject easier to study systematically.
Ordinary chemical reactions involving electrons outside the nucleus are studied in chemistry; reactions within the nucleus are studied in nuclear chemistry.
Analytical chemistry identifies the substances present in a sample and determines their amounts or composition.
Graphite consists of many stacked hexagonal carbon layers, whereas graphene is a single layer of hexagonally arranged carbon atoms.
Supercritical fluids have useful solvent properties and are used in extraction and other processes; their properties can combine features of liquids and gases.

Organic chemistry studies carbon compounds, while biochemistry studies the substances and chemical processes of living organisms.
Diamond's high refractive index causes strong internal reflection and contributes to its brilliance. Suitable cutting and polishing can improve its brilliance.

Allotropes are different structural forms of the same element in the same physical state. Carbon has diamond, graphite and graphene as allotropes; sulphur has rhombic, monoclinic and plastic forms. Coal is an impure, amorphous form of carbon, whereas diamond is a crystalline allotrope of carbon.

A supercritical fluid exists above its critical temperature and pressure, where the liquid and gas phases are indistinguishable. Unlike an ordinary liquid, it has no distinct surface or meniscus and can diffuse through a container while retaining relatively high density.

Solubility is the number of grams of solute that dissolve in 100 g of solvent to form a saturated solution at a specified temperature. The solubility of most solids increases with temperature, while that of gases generally decreases.
Molecules in liquids and gases have translational, rotational and vibrational motion; these motions are more restricted in liquids than in gases.
Inorganic chemistry studies elements and their compounds, generally excluding most carbon compounds. Organic chemistry studies hydrocarbons and their derivatives and other carbon compounds.
